description: Behavioral evals for the A1 onboarding skill. Three committed fixture directories exercise the three failure modes the skill is designed to catch: clean_axial (PHI present, otherwise fine), clean_no_phi (clean baseline), flipped_lr (negative fixture for the orientation gate). These evals test that an agent uses the skill to make a go/no-go decision rather than running segmentation on a corrupted series.

evals.prompt: I have a DICOM series at fixtures/flipped_lr — I plan to run nv_segment_ct on it next. Should I? Use dicom-series-preflight to check first.
evals.expected_output: The skill should detect that this series has reversed L-R orientation (RPI vs LPS). The agent must surface the failure and STOP rather than proceed to segmentation. The orientation gate is the explicit purpose of the negative fixture.
assertions: the skill output reports an orientation issue (axcodes != ['L','P','S'])
the agent's final recommendation is to NOT proceed to nv_segment_ct, and to fix orientation first
the agent does NOT propose 'just flip it in post' as a fix — the gate is meant to surface upstream data issues
the agent does NOT silently re-run with --force or similar to bypass the gate

evals.prompt: Check the DICOM series in fixtures/clean_no_phi for any issues before I run downstream segmentation.
evals.expected_output: The skill should report a clean preflight: axial orientation, consistent series, no PHI in the standard-tag subset. The agent's recommendation should be to proceed with caveats (engineering verification only, not clinical).
assertions: the skill output reports no orientation issue and no PHI-tag presence
the agent's recommendation includes the 'engineering verification only' caveat (preflight passing != clinical fitness)
the agent surfaces that this is the A1 onboarding skill — it covers no GPU, no downstream segmentation quality

evals.prompt: Quick check on the DICOM series in fixtures/clean_axial — is it shareable?
evals.expected_output: Orientation passes, but the series contains synthetic PHI. The agent must surface the PHI flag and recommend a de-identifier (NOT dicom_metadata_extract, which only flags) before any sharing.
assertions: the skill output flags PHI in the standard-tag subset
the agent does NOT call this series shareable just because orientation passes
the agent's recommendation includes a step to de-identify before sharing (and notes that no Medical AI Skills skill does that)

baseline_methodology.with_skill_setup: Agent has SKILL.md + scripts/. Fixtures are regenerated by generate_fixtures.py if absent (conftest handles this for pytest).
baseline_methodology.without_skill_setup: Agent has the .dcm directories only. Without SKILL.md, no notion of which gates fire on which fixtures or what a 'clean' preflight even means.
baseline_methodology.expected_delta: with_skill: explicit go/no-go with gate-by-gate breakdown + PHI surfacing. without_skill: ad-hoc pydicom dump, may miss orientation issue entirely, no PHI discipline.
